subject: stacked bar plot to avoid a pie plot

messages.subject: stacked bar plot to avoid a pie plot
parts:
Dear list members,

I am trying to make a bar plot to avoid a pie plot.  I want a stacked bar graph, but only one bar in the plot. 

df = data.frame(x=c(18, 8, 10),   
     factor= c("Dependencia alta", "Dependencia media", "Dependencia baja"))
df

p = ggplot(df, aes(factor, x))
p + geom_bar()

Best,

Manuel

messages.subject: Re: stacked bar plot to avoid a pie plot
parts:
Manuel,

I don't know how to create a stacked bar chart in ggplot2, and I would like to suggest looking for other solutions.

Stacked bar charts make it very difficult to compare the values of each category that has been stacked. Suppose, for example, that you want to compare "Dependencia alta," "Dependencia media" and "Dependencia baja" to each other. At best, you can only approximately determine the ranking (largest to smallest); the stacking defeats our ability to use the axis to look up the actual values. Similarly, if you wanted to compare the three values across some third variable, perhaps years, then a stacked bar chart would allow you to compare the total of the three across years, but your readers will be limited to making only very general, qualitative comparisons of each category across the years, and therefore would come away with a limited understanding of how "Dependencia alta" has changed over time.

You might consider using a dot plot instead:
p + geom_point() + coord_flip()

and then using facets to group the dot plots in a suitable manner.

Regards,

Tom Hopper
